input.strategy_title: Adopt structured JSON logging across RHOAI components
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

RHOAI components log in inconsistent formats — plain text, key=value, and
ad-hoc JSON — which breaks centralized log queries and makes support cases
expensive: correlating one user request across Dashboard, serving, and
pipelines requires per-component parsing rules. The platform needs one
structured logging convention, and each component needs to adopt it. Component
adoptions are independent of each other once the convention exists.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1  | P0 | A platform logging convention is published: JSON schema, required fields (timestamp, level, component, namespace, correlation id), and library guidance per language (Go, Python, TypeScript). |
| HLR-2  | P0 | Dashboard emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-3  | P0 | KServe controller and serving runtimes emit convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-4  | P1 | Data Science Pipelines (operator and API server) emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-5  | P1 | Model Registry emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-6  | P1 | TrustyAI services emit convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-7  | P1 | Notebooks (notebook-controller) emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-8  | P2 | Training Operator emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-9  | P2 | Documentation describes the log format and example queries for common support scenarios. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- KServe
- Data Science Pipelines
- Model Registry
- TrustyAI
- Notebooks
- Training Operator

## Out of Scope

- Log storage, retention, or forwarding infrastructure
- Metrics and tracing conventions (logging only)

## Open Questions

None — the convention work (HLR-1) is prerequisite design, and per-component
adoptions are mechanical once it lands.

# Platform structured logging convention

## Description

This epic delivers the platform-wide structured logging convention that all
RHOAI components will adopt: a published JSON log-record schema, the set of
required fields, and per-language library guidance. It is prerequisite design
work — every component adoption builds against this artifact.

## Scope

- Define and publish the JSON schema for platform log records.
- Specify the required fields: timestamp, level, component, namespace, and
  correlation id, including their formats and semantics.
- Provide library guidance per supported language: Go, Python, and TypeScript
  (recommended logging libraries and how to emit convention-conformant records
  with them).
- Validate the guidance against each affected component's existing logging
  stack so that adoption is mechanical once the convention lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The convention is published and available to all component teams.
- The JSON schema defines every required field (timestamp, level, component,
  namespace, correlation id) with format and semantics.
- Library guidance exists for Go, Python, and TypeScript.
- A log record conforming to the schema can be validated mechanically
  (schema-validatable), so adoption compliance is checkable in CI or review.
- Representatives of the affected component teams have reviewed the
  convention, or review has been requested and documented.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): A platform logging convention is published: JSON schema,
  required fields, and library guidance per language.

# Dashboard structured logging adoption

## Description

The RHOAI Dashboard emits convention-conformant structured JSON logs: every log
record the Dashboard services produce is valid per the platform logging
convention, with the required fields populated, so a user request can be
correlated across the platform without Dashboard-specific parsing rules.

## Scope

- Replace the Dashboard's current log output (plain text / key=value / ad-hoc
  JSON) with records conforming to the published platform logging convention.
- Populate the required fields — timestamp, level, component, namespace, and
  correlation id — on every emitted record, propagating the correlation id
  from available request context.
- Preserve existing diagnostic content (messages, error details); the format
  changes, the information does not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All Dashboard service logs are valid JSON records conforming to the platform
  logging convention schema.
- Every record carries the required fields: timestamp, level, component,
  namespace, correlation id (correlation id populated wherever request context
  is available).
- A single user request can be followed through Dashboard logs using the
  correlation id alone, with no Dashboard-specific parsing rules.
- The log format change is revertible (configuration flag or documented
  rollback path) so existing log consumers are not broken during transition.
- No diagnostic information present in the previous log output is lost.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Dashboard emits convention-conformant logs.

# KServe controller structured logging adoption

## Description

The KServe controller (the RHOAI KServe midstream) emits convention-conformant
structured JSON logs, so controller lifecycle and reconciliation events can be
queried centrally and correlated with requests seen in other platform
components.

## Scope

- Replace the KServe controller's current log output with records conforming
  to the published platform logging convention, using the Go library guidance
  from the convention.
- Populate the required fields — timestamp, level, component, namespace, and
  correlation id — on every emitted record, deriving namespace and component
  from the reconciled resource where applicable.
- Preserve existing diagnostic content (reconciliation messages, error
  details).

## Acceptance Criteria

- All KServe controller logs are valid JSON records conforming to the platform
  logging convention schema.
- Every record carries the required fields: timestamp, level, component,
  namespace, correlation id.
- Controller events for a given resource can be queried by namespace and
  correlation id without KServe-specific parsing rules.
- The log format change is revertible (configuration flag or documented
  rollback path) so existing log consumers are not broken during transition.
- No diagnostic information present in the previous log output is lost.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P0, KServe controller portion): KServe controller and serving
  runtimes emit convention-conformant logs.

# Serving runtimes structured logging adoption

## Description

The RHOAI serving runtimes (vLLM, OpenVINO, Caikit) emit convention-conformant
structured JSON logs, so model serving request logs can be correlated with the
same request observed in the Dashboard and elsewhere in the platform.

## Scope

- Bring each serving runtime's log output into conformance with the published
  platform logging convention, following the convention's library guidance for
  each runtime's language.
- Populate the required fields — timestamp, level, component, namespace, and
  correlation id — on every emitted record, propagating the correlation id
  from inference request context where available.
- Preserve existing diagnostic content.

## Assumptions and Risks

- The serving runtimes are upstream projects consumed by the platform.
  Adoption is expected to land via the existing midstream change process; if
  midstream patching proves untenable for a runtime, upstream coordination
  may be required — the strategy characterizes all adoptions as mechanical,
  and this assumption should be revisited if it does not hold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Logs emitted by each serving runtime are valid JSON records conforming to
  the platform logging convention schema.
- Every record carries the required fields: timestamp, level, component,
  namespace, correlation id (correlation id populated wherever inference
  request context is available).
- A model serving request can be correlated across Dashboard and serving
  runtime logs using the correlation id alone.
- The log format change is revertible (configuration flag or documented
  rollback path) so existing log consumers are not broken during transition.
- No diagnostic information present in the previous log output is lost.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P0, serving runtimes portion): KServe controller and serving
  runtimes emit convention-conformant logs.
